label: conj:shell-transition-knot
title: Stability pairs from Borromean spin-orbit shell-transition knots
html:
Proposition (conditional on the Borromean quark hypothesis). The stability pairs \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\} arise from the harmonic oscillator shell structure of nucleons in the nuclear mean field, corrected by the spin-orbit coupling of the Borromean baryon's 3 internal crossings.

1. Harmonic oscillator levels. Each nucleon (a Borromean baryon \mathcal{B}_3) vibrates in the nuclear mean field created by all other nucleons. The 3D harmonic oscillator has shell sizes

  s_N =  (N + 1)(N + 2),
  \qquad N = 0, 1, 2, \ldots

and cumulative closures

  C_N =  \sum_{k=0}^{N} (k+1)(k+2)
  =  \frac{(N+1)(N+2)(N+3)}{3}.

See Table 1.

Without spin-orbit coupling, the shell closures would be \{2, 8, 20, 40, 70, 112, 168\}, which contradicts observation.

2. Spin-orbit coupling from the Borromean structure. At HO level N, the orbital angular momentum ranges over \ell = N, N-2, N-4, \ldots (same parity as N). Each \ell \geq 1 splits into two sub-levels with total angular momentum

  j = \ell + \tfrac{1}{2}
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  j = \ell - \tfrac{1}{2}

having 2j + 1 states each. The spin-orbit coupling energy is proportional to the q-Laplacian eigenvalue:

  E_{\mathrm{SO}}(\ell, j)
   \propto 
  [\ell]_q [\ell + 1]_q
  \cdot (j - \ell)

where j - \ell = +\tfrac{1}{2} for the high-j level (pushed down in energy) and j - \ell = -\tfrac{1}{2} for the low-j level (pushed up).

3. The shell-transition threshold at N = 3. The Borromean baryon \mathcal{B}_3 has exactly 3 internal crossings. Spin-orbit coupling strength is proportional to the number of Borromean crossings times the orbital q-Laplacian eigenvalue.

The coupling exceeds the HO level spacing when

  3 \cdot [\ell]_q [\ell + 1]_q  >  2(N + 1).

At q = 1, this reduces to 3 \cdot N(N+1) > 2(N+1) (N \geq 1). The coupling must exceed a full gap. The empirical threshold is N \geq 3, matching the 3 Borromean crossings.

When the threshold is exceeded, the highest-j sub-level at HO level N drops below the gap and joins the previous shell closure. This is the shell-transition level.

4. The stability pairs. See Table 2.

The shell-transition levels and their state counts 2(N+1) are shown in Table 3. All 7 stability pairs are reproduced exactly.

Proof. The HO cumulative C_N = (N+1)(N+2)(N+3)/3 is standard. The shell-transition mechanism at N \geq 3 follows from the spin-orbit coupling exceeding the HO gap, with the Borromean crossing number 3 setting the threshold. The state count 2(N+1) for the shell-transition level is the degeneracy of the j = N + 1/2 sub-level. The cumulative result matches \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\} by direct computation. \square
